chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The fasting person immerses himself in the water and does not rub his head.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on rubbing the head while performing ghusl in water while fasting?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani’s *al-Istibsar* clarifies the ritual etiquette for a fasting person performing *ghusl* (major ablution) in water, specifically permitting full submersion while advising against vigorously rubbing the head (*ramus*). Scholars interpret this distinction as a precaution to prevent the accidental swallowing of water or to maintain the integrity of the fast, reflecting the nuanced juristic approach to ritual purity in Shia fiqh. The narration highlights the practical application of *ghusl* rules, emphasizing that the act of washing the head does not inherently break the fast unless specific conditions are met.
